title: Bato dela Rosa's world getting smaller as authorities step up manhunt ops --Palace
summary: Malacañang on Thursday defended anew the P50 million bounty set on Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa"s head, saying that his world has gotten smaller as authorities have stepped up efforts to arrest…

blocks.text: Malacañang on Thursday defended anew the P50 million bounty set on Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa’s head, saying that his world has gotten smaller as authorities have stepped up efforts to arrest him.

“Totoo na lumiliit ang mundo ni Senator Bato dahil ang maaaring makakita sa kaniya ay magbibigay ng impormasyon agad-agad sa PNP at sa ibang law enforcement agencies,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in a press briefing.
(It is true that Senator Bato’s world is getting smaller because whoever sees him could give information immediately to the PNP and other law enforcement agencies.)
Reading a statement from the Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG) and the Philippine National Police (PNP), Castro said that the agencies have stepped up their manhunt for Dela Rosa.

“The combined effect of heightened police operations increase public awareness and the bounty announcement has substantially narrowed the senator's ability to move freely without drawing attention,” Castro said, reading the joint statement.
“We likewise appeal to Senator Dela Rosa to voluntarily surrender to the proper authorities and submit himself to the legal process with dignity,” she added.
However, she did not disclosure more details regarding the operations.
Castro said that all information being received is carefully reviewed and credible leads are being acted upon.
The task force, led by Police Lieutenant General Wilson Joseph Lopez, is currently ensuring seamless coordination among all concerned agencies, she added.
The Palace official also emphasized that the P50 million bounty for Dela Rosa came from the confidential funds of the DILG.

Dela Rosa’s camp has sought the intervention of the Supreme Court in the manhunt against him in relation arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court. He sought a temporary restraining order to prevent the government from arresting him. —AOL, GMA News
